sections.html:
This is the only real freshwater species of moray: Gymnothorax polyuranodon. Usually this species is not found over 30-40 km away from the coast, but most often in pure freshwater. The other salt tolerant species of moray, for example Gymnothorax tile, usually do not leave the tidal zone.

Maximum length reported for this species is about 150 cm. Each single specimen has an individual pattern of spots.
This species is only very rarely available despite its wide distribution in the Indo-West Pacific region. It has now been imported from Indonesia as juveniles 20-25 cm long.
The pH is important: it should never be on the acidic side, but always over 7.5, better over 8.

In respect of keeping morays in the aquarium one has to take care that the tank is absolutely closely covered. Morays will find even the smallest gap and press their body through – often with a fatal consequence.

For feeding one should place some live small feeder fish of about guppy size in the moray tank. When these feeder fish are vanished the morays have started feeding. However, the keeper has to be patient. Often enough this takes several days to weeks. The fasting is usually harmless for the morays.
In the aquarium these morays are very anxious during settlement. So they should be kept along only with absolutely peaceful and calm fish.
Breeding appears only in the sea – like in all species of moray. This is the reason why the species is so far spread, as the eggs and the larvae are taken away with the currents.
